title: देश भर में मॉनसून का कहर: दिल्ली से लेकर यूपी, बिहार और पहाड़ी राज्यों तक भारी बारिश का अलर्ट - bhaskardigital.com
article_text:
देशभर के कई राज्यों में इन दिनों मॉनसून जमकर बरस रहा है। उत्तर भारत के राज्यों में लगातार बारिश का सिलसिला जारी है, जबकि पूर्वी भारत में भी बादल झमाझम बरस रहे हैं। उत्तर भारत के इलाकों में जहां मॉनसून ने फिर से जोर पकड़ लिया है, वहीं ओडिशा, पश्चिम बंगाल और झारखंड में डीप डिप्रेशन की वजह से बारिश थमने का नाम नहीं ले रही है। मौसम विभाग के पूर्वानुमान के मुताबिक, बारिश का यह दौर अभी और अधिक तीव्र होने वाला है।
देश की राजधानी दिल्ली में मॉनसून एक बार फिर पूरी तरह सक्रिय दिखाई दे रहा है। मौसम विभाग की ओर से आज राज्य में आमतौर पर बादल छाए रहने और मध्यम दर्जे की बारिश होने की संभावना जताई गई है। इसके अलावा, आगामी दिनों यानी 21, 22 और 23 अगस्त को भी राज्य में हल्की बारिश और बूंदाबांदी का दौर जारी रहने के आसार हैं। वहीं, आज दिल्ली का अधिकतम तापमान 33 डिग्री और न्यूनतम तापमान 26 डिग्री सेल्सियस के आसपास दर्ज किया जा सकता है।
उत्तर प्रदेश में इन दिनों मॉनसून पूरी तरह मेहरबान है। आज प्रदेश के मुजफ्फरनगर, मेरठ, गौतमबुद्ध नगर, मथुरा, आगरा, अलीगढ़, हमीरपुर, जालौन, झांसी, ललितपुर, बांदा, फतेहपुर, कानपुर, इटावा, आजमगढ़, प्रतापगढ़, चित्रकूट, प्रयागराज, देवरिया और गोरखपुर में भारी बारिश के साथ आंधी-तूफान का अलर्ट जारी किया गया है।
बिहार के भी कई जिलों में भारी बारिश और तेज हवाओं की चेतावनी दी गई है, जबकि झारखंड में आज और कल तेज हवाओं के साथ झमाझम बारिश का प्रभाव लगातार बना रहेगा। पश्चिम बंगाल के कई जिलों में आज भारी आंधी-तूफान के साथ भारी बारिश होने की संभावना है।
इसके अलावा, ओडिशा में मॉनसून के पूरी तरह सक्रिय रहने के कारण 21 से 25 अगस्त के दौरान व्यापक पैमाने पर बारिश हो सकती है। राजस्थान के कई हिस्सों में आज आंधी और बारिश देखने को मिल सकती है, और मध्य प्रदेश के तमाम जिलों में भी भारी बारिश का येलो/ऑरेंज अलर्ट है। पंजाब और हरियाणा में भी आज और कल तेज हवाओं के साथ अचानक बारिश जोर पकड़ सकती है।
उधर पश्चिमी भारत की बात करें तो कोंकण और गोवा में 25 अगस्त तक भारी बारिश का अनुमान जताया गया है। मध्य महाराष्ट्र और मराठवाड़ा में आज बारिश की गतिविधियों में काफी तेजी आने की संभावना है। गुजरात और सौराष्ट्र-कच्छ के कुछ इलाकों में भी 25 अगस्त तक छिटपुट से लेकर अच्छी बारिश हो सकती है।
पूर्वोत्तर राज्यों की बात करें तो अरुणाचल प्रदेश, असम, मेघालय के साथ-साथ नागालैंड, मणिपुर, मिजोरम और त्रिपुरा में भी बारिश का सिलसिला जारी रहेगा। इनमें से अरुणाचल प्रदेश, असम और मेघालय में 25 अगस्त तक कुछ स्थानों पर मूसलाधार बारिश की संभावना है। दक्षिण भारत के केरल, कर्नाटक और तेलंगाना में भी आंधी के साथ बारिश की चेतावनी दी गई है, जबकि तमिलनाडु के कई इलाकों में भारी बारिश हो सकती है।
पहाड़ी क्षेत्रों में भी मौसम के कड़े तेवर देखने को मिल रहे हैं। उत्तराखंड के नैनीताल, हरिद्वार, ऋषिकेश, बागेश्वर, अल्मोड़ा, पिथौरागढ़, पौड़ी गढ़वाल, चंपावत, रुद्रप्रयाग और ऊधम सिंह नगर जैसे जिलों में भारी बारिश और तेज आंधी का अलर्ट जारी किया गया है। इसके अलावा, हिमाचल प्रदेश और जम्मू-कश्मीर के कई जिलों में भी मौसम विभाग ने आंधी-तूफान के साथ भारी बारिश की चेतावनी दी है, जिसे देखते हुए प्रशासन ने लोगों को सतर्क रहने की सलाह दी है।

title: India Monsoon Disaster: Rajouri Counts Its Dead, Uttarakhand on Alert, Assam Struggles to Rebuild After Floods - openthemagazine.com
article_text:
In Rajouri, a family of six sleeps inside a government school after watching its house disappear. In Uttarakhand, officials are pulling residents out of vulnerable homes and warning pilgrims to step away from swollen rivers. In Assam, flood survivors have returned to rooms buried under silt, empty granaries and appliances destroyed by water.
Three states are confronting three stages of the same monsoon disaster: destruction, danger and the long struggle to rebuild.
A cloudburst over the hilly Rajdhani Panchayat in Jammu and Kashmir’s Rajouri district triggered flash floods and landslides that killed four people on July 19, swept away houses and vehicles and tore through roads and farmland.
Residents reported intense bursts of rain and flooding at about 14 locations across the area. Water thundered through local streams, carrying boulders and debris towards settlements below. The main bus stand was washed away. Vehicles vanished into the current. Roads cracked, cultivated land disappeared and landslides scarred the hills.

The wider spell of extreme weather killed at least 15 people across Poonch, Rajouri and Doda districts, a senior police official told Reuters after the disaster.
For Abdul Gani’s family, the warning arrived as sound. “We were all inside our house when we heard the roar of the river and the crashing of rolling boulders,” he recalled. The family scrambled out before the torrent swallowed its home. With their possessions gone and the area initially difficult to reach, all six members moved into a government school. “Earlier, the water used to rise only a little bit,” Gani said. “This time it came in huge volumes.”
One month later, the July 19 flood has left Rajdhani with damaged roads, unstable slopes and families trying to rebuild without the homes or farmland that sustained them. Residents have described the flood as unlike anything they had witnessed before. However, reports of a cloudburst at multiple points would require meteorological verification. In mountainous terrain, extremely intense local rain can overwhelm streams within minutes even when gauges fail to capture its precise location or volume.
While Rajouri examines what the water took, Uttarakhand is trying to prevent the next tragedy.
Continuous rain across the Garhwal region has swollen rivers, damaged roads and forced the administration to move residents away from vulnerable houses. Garhwal Commissioner Anand Swaroop said some locations had recorded more than 200mm of rain in a day. Water levels have climbed in major rivers, including the Tons, Asan and Tamsa, while the Rispana is carrying increased flows from the hills.
Authorities have ordered repeated public announcements asking people to stay away from riverbanks. The warning includes a deceptively ordinary modern risk: stopping near raging water to take photographs or selfies. Char Dham pilgrims have been told to obey local restrictions and wait in designated holding areas whenever routes are temporarily closed. District magistrates can halt movement for several hours when rainfall, landslides or damaged roads make travel unsafe. Around 8,000 to 9,000 pilgrims continue to visit the shrines daily, according to the Garhwal administration. Holding areas equipped with toilets and drinking water have been created for travellers stranded by temporary suspensions.
The India Meteorological Department has forecast isolated heavy rain over Uttarakhand through August 24, along with thunderstorms and lightning. Its Char Dham pilgrimage forecast also indicates the possibility of rain and thunderstorms along the routes.
The Yatra remains operational, but “operational” does not mean uninterrupted. In the mountains, a safe road in the morning can be blocked by a landslide before the next group of pilgrims arrives. The administration expects another surge of visitors when the second phase of the pilgrimage gathers momentum after September 15. That leaves officials balancing religious travel against a landscape already saturated by weeks of rain.
Assam’s survivors face a different emergency.
In several parts of Sivasagar, floodwater has receded only to expose homes packed with mud, broken furniture and rotting food. Some low-lying areas remain inundated. Families unable to return are staying with relatives or paying rent for temporary rooms.
One resident lost 20 quintals of stored grain when the water surged into the house. The refrigerator and other belongings were ruined. “The water rose quickly, so we’ve lost everything,” the resident said.
The family initially sheltered with others before moving into rented accommodation. When members returned to clean the house, little remained to salvage. “Everything is destroyed, absolutely everything is gone,” the resident said.
The July floods killed more than 100 people across Assam and displaced over 700,000, according to the Associated Press. At the height of the crisis, nearly 300,000 people entered government-run shelters. Tens of thousands remained in relief camps even after rivers began retreating.
The Assam government recently released ₹47.93 crore in interim assistance to 31,951 flood-hit families across Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat and Golaghat. Each family received ₹15,000, taking the state’s total distributed assistance to ₹146.26 crore, The Economic Times reported.
But a transfer cannot immediately replace a home, a crop, livestock or grain accumulated over years. Flood recovery begins after the television images end. Wells must be cleaned. Silt must be shovelled out. Walls need to dry before they can be repaired. Families must replace documents, utensils, beds and schoolbooks while finding money for food and rent.
The weather threat has not passed. The IMD has forecast heavy rainfall at isolated places over Jammu and Kashmir, Uttarakhand and Assam, among several other regions. Saturated slopes can collapse after subsequent rain, while rivers can rise rapidly when intense downpours occur upstream.
The three states also reveal why a flood cannot be measured only by the height of the water or the death toll recorded that day. Rajouri shows how quickly extreme rain can erase a settlement. Uttarakhand shows why warnings, route closures and early evacuation matter before a river breaks its banks. Assam shows what remains when the water finally retreats: mud, debt, displacement and the slow work of putting a life back together. The cloud may burst in minutes. The flood can last for months.
A cloudburst over Rajdhani Panchayat in Rajouri district on July 19 triggered flash floods and landslides, killing four people and sweeping away houses and roads.
Uttarakhand is on alert due to continuous rain, causing rivers to swell and damaging roads. Officials are moving residents and warning Char Dham pilgrims about unsafe conditions.
Pilgrims are advised to stay away from riverbanks and obey local restrictions. Routes may close due to landslides or rain, with holding areas available for stranded travelers.

title: Travel Alert: IMD Issues Orange Warning for Heavy Rain and Thunderstorms Across Southern and Central India - NativePlanet
article_text:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued fresh weather warnings for several regions today. Heavy rainfall and severe thunderstorms are expected across southern and central belts. Kerala, coastal Karnataka, Odisha, and Chhattisgarh remain under active orange watch. Commuters should expect disrupted travel schedules and potential waterlogging in urban hotspots.
Weather forecasters are monitoring real-time changes through strict three-hour nowcast updates. Key tracking slots include 08:30, 11:30, 14:30, and 17:30 IST. Strong surface winds reaching up to sixty kilometers per hour are expected. Sudden lightning bursts pose severe safety risks during peak afternoon travel hours. Travelers must track live updates before heading outside.
Subtropical monsoon systems are driving intense rainfall over coastal Karnataka and Kerala. Meanwhile, Chhattisgarh and Odisha face prolonged downpours caused by active low-pressure troughs. Heavy precipitation increases flash flood hazards in low-lying residential regions. Local administrations urge residents to stay indoors during heavy spells. Plan transit routes carefully to avoid sudden road blockages.
Air travel and rail operations may experience delays near coastal and central airport hubs. Urban commuters face waterlogged roads, slow traffic, and potential public transport suspensions. Passengers should consult airline advisories before leaving for the airport. Traffic police departments continuously publish live route updates online to assist commuters.
Checking verified weather sources helps citizens avoid hazardous road conditions and sudden storms. The State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA) issues regular location-based safety bulletins. People can monitor live Doppler radar maps on official meteorological portals. Cross-referencing traffic police alerts ensures smoother and safer daily travel decisions.
Staying informed remains vital as wet weather patterns persist across key southern and central corridors. Commuters and travelers should keep emergency contact numbers accessible throughout the day. Adhering to official warnings reduces transit risks during unexpected thunderstorm activity.

title: Heavy rain brings relief to Delhi amid active northern monsoon - thenewsmill.com
article_text:
Heavy rain fell across parts of Delhi on Thursday, providing relief from hot and humid weather for residents. The downpour was accompanied by persistent cloudy skies over much of the city.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecast light rain between 12:30 pm and 3:30 pm, with temperatures remaining around 33 degrees Celsius and a 20 per cent chance of rainfall. The likelihood of rain was expected to increase in the evening, with scattered thunderstorms predicted from 4:30 pm to 6:30 pm. During this period, temperatures were anticipated to remain between 31 and 32 degrees Celsius, with a 35 per cent chance of rain.

The monsoon remains active across several states in northern and eastern India. Heavy rainfall was reported in Himachal Pradesh, Assam, Gujarat, Odisha, Uttarakhand, and Uttar Pradesh, prompting IMD to issue colour-coded alerts for heavy to extremely heavy rainfall and related risks.

In Uttar Pradesh, red alerts have been declared for extremely heavy rainfall in districts including Banda, Prayagraj, and Mirzapur, while multiple neighbouring districts are under yellow alerts. Himachal Pradesh has experienced persistent heavy rain and adverse weather disrupting daily life. The State Emergency Operation Centre reported 166 road blockages, including National Highway-003, and noted that 130 power transformers and 222 water supply schemes have been affected. Mandi district has been most severely impacted, with 84 roads blocked.

ADVERTISEMENT

Kerala authorities have issued a red alert for the coast along with a Swell Surge and High Wave Warning covering the coasts of Kerala, Lakshadweep, South Tamil Nadu, and Puducherry. Coastal areas are expected to experience rough seas, with swell waves between 1.1 and 2.2 metres. Fishermen have been advised against venturing into the sea, and restrictions have been placed on operations of small fishing vessels, boat movements, and beach activities.

In Odisha, officials continue to monitor areas affected by flooding amid forecasts of further heavy rain. As of August 15, 429 villages across 52 blocks had been impacted by floodwaters, and 79 rescue teams deployed. The Central Water Commission has issued warnings of flash-flood risks in parts of the state.

title: IMD issues red alert for extremely heavy rainfall in Gangetic West Bengal and Odisha tomorrow - News On AIR
article_text:
India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red colour warning for very heavy rainfall to extremely heavy rainfall over Jharkhand for tomorrow. The Weather Agency forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall over Bihar, Chhattisgarh, East Madhya Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Odisha and West Uttar Pradesh tomorrow. According to IMD, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Chandigarh, Haryana, Delhi, East Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Sikkim, North Eastern States, Karaikal, Puducherry, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Mahe will experience heavy rainfall till Thursday. The Met Department also predicted thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds over Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka and Andaman and Nicobar Islands for next two to three days.

IMD has advised fishermen to not venture into Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal till tomorrow.
